convention: transaction k (1-based) of a scenario is mined at timestamp 1791582443 + 12*k; every scenario starts from the same snapshot of the source block
assumptions: Local fork: no transaction is sent to Ethereum
Impersonated actors: scenario hypothesis, not their signature or intention
Oracle overrides (hardhat_setCode with a constant price) and liquidator funding (hardhat_setStorageAt / wrapped ETH) are shock hypotheses

scenario.title: Incident: RLP Price AggregatorV3 interface -10%, liquidations limited by AMM depth measured at the block, then the largest competing holders exit first
hypotheses: Contracts and state are real at the source block; transactions are simulated on a local fork, never sent to Ethereum.
Shock hypothesis: the oracle contract is replaced on the fork by one returning the shocked price.
Every unhealthy borrower is liquidated by a liquidator with enough loan tokens (impersonated).
Other holders are impersonated on a local fork: their exits are a scenario hypothesis, not their signature or intention.
Only the borrowers whose collateral the measured AMM depth absorbs at a profit are liquidated.
